study.title: Localization of brain networks activated by acupuncture at anatomically adjacent acupoints in healthy participants: neuroimaging evidence and implications for migraine and stroke
study.study_design: Systematic review with functional connectivity network mapping (FCNM) meta-analysis; integrates activation coordinates from included fMRI studies in healthy controls with large-scale resting-state connectome datasets
study.population: Healthy controls (HCs) from included fMRI studies and connectome datasets
study.disease_condition: Healthy participants; implications discussed for migraine and stroke
study.inclusion_criteria: (1) They had to include HCs only; (2) They needed to report findings related to ST36, GB34; (3) They had to report findings in 3D coordinates in either the Montreal Neurological Institute (MNI) space or Talairach space; (4) They had to incorporate whole-brain signaling analysis.
study.exclusion_criteria: (1) Did not include a HCs group; (2) Investigated only region of interest (ROI) results or used analytical methods such as functional connectivity, independent component analysis, or graph theory; (3) Consisted of reviews, case reports, conference abstracts, or animal studies; (4) Did not report peak effect coordinates; (5) Were not available in full text; (6) Had a sample size of fewer than 10 participants were excluded in FCNM analysis.

neuroimaging_methods.normalization_template_exact: Montreal Neurological Institute (MNI) space via deformation fields derived from structural image segmentation
neuroimaging_methods.smoothing_exact: Gaussian kernel with a 6 mm full-width at half maximum
neuroimaging_methods.motion_exclusion_exact: Participants exhibiting excessive head motion—defined as translational displacement greater than 2.0 mm or rotational motion exceeding 2.0° were excluded from the analysis. Additional exclusions were applied in cases of incomplete brain coverage or suboptimal image quality.
neuroimaging_methods.filtering_exact: band-pass filtering within the 0.01–0.08 Hz frequency range
neuroimaging_methods.global_signal_regression_exact: regression of nuisance covariates, including Friston-24 motion parameters, white matter signal, cerebrospinal fluid signal, and global signal
primary_neuroimaging_metrics: Functional connectivity (FC) — Pearson's correlation coefficients between contrast seed time series and whole-brain voxels, Fisher's z-transformed
FCNM network probability maps thresholded at 60%

statistical_thresholds_exact: P < 0.01, corrected for multiple comparisons using a voxel-wise false discovery rate (FDR) procedure

funding_conflicts_registration.ethics_approval_exact: The neuroimaging data used in this study were obtained from the 1000 Functional Connectomes Project (FCP) database (http://www.nitrc.org/projects/fcon_1000/). The FCP is an aggregated, fully anonymized dataset pooled from multiple independent sites worldwide. As clearly stated on the FCP portal, all contributing sites obtained local institutional review board (IRB) approval and informed consent from all participants prior to data collection and sharing. Since the data are fully preprocessed and de-identified, and our analysis involved only secondary use of this public dataset, this study did not require additional ethics approval from our institutional review board.
funding_conflicts_registration.data_availability_exact: The original contributions presented in this study are included in this article/Supplementary material, further inquiries can be directed to the corresponding authors.

extraction_notes.note: This is a systematic review and FCNM meta-analysis. No primary acupuncture procedures were conducted by the authors. Intervention details (needle type, size, depth, manipulation, deqi, session number, retention time) pertain to the included primary studies and are not uniformly reported for individual included studies in the main text. Supplementary Tables 1 and 2 reportedly contain these details but were not provided in the PDF.

Sensory/interoceptive responses (deqi, pain, etc.) were not measured or reported as outcomes in this study. The study aggregates published fMRI coordinate data from primary studies and does not report sensory data.
Clinical/behavioral outcomes were not assessed in this study. It is a neuroimaging systematic review and FCNM analysis only.
Expectancy, blinding, credibility, and allocation guessing data were not reported. No placebo or sham arm was included.
Adverse events were not reported. This is a secondary data analysis / systematic review with no primary patient contact.
Specific MRI scanning parameters (TR, TE, sequence) for the SLIM and FCP datasets are reported to be in Supplementary Table 3 but were not provided in the PDF.

The exact coordinates of all brain regions comprising the ST36 and GB34 FCNM networks are not provided in the main text as tabular coordinate data. Brain regions are described narratively (e.g., precentral gyrus, postcentral gyrus, precuneus, etc.) but peak MNI coordinates for each region are not reported. Coordinates are only visible in Figures 3 and 4 (probability maps shown as brain slices), which cannot be numerically extracted from the PDF.

The FCNM probability maps for ST36 (Figure 3) and GB34 (Figure 4) are presented as brain slice images with color-coded probability thresholds (60%-90%). No coordinate tables are provided in the main text or supplement for these maps. Specific MNI coordinates for identified regions cannot be extracted.

The included primary studies had heterogeneous designs: 28 used manual acupuncture, 6 used electroacupuncture, and 1 used moxibustion. The FCNM pooled coordinates across all these modalities without stratification. This is a source of heterogeneity noted in the extraction.

The paper uses 'NAT' and 'NET' interchangeably. In Table 1 for ST36, the label is 'NET'; in the text of Section 4.3, it is 'NAT'; for GB34 in Table 1, the label is 'NAT'. The abstract uses 'noradrenaline transporter (NET)'. These appear to refer to the same neurotransmitter transporter. Values have been extracted using the exact label appearing in Table 1 for each acupoint.

Figure 5 caption states both panels B and D are 'The spatial correlation between ST36 network and neurotransmitter density maps.' Panel D appears to be mislabeled in the caption and should read 'GB34 network.' The neurotransmitter correlation results for GB34 are correctly described in Section 4.4 and Table 1.

The sample size of 573 participants refers to the SLIM discovery dataset used for FCNM connectivity mapping, not to the participants in the included acupuncture fMRI studies (513 for ST36; 112 for GB34). These are distinct populations serving different roles in the analysis.

Supplementary Figure 1 (sensitivity analysis of task-fMRI based study) and Supplementary Tables 1, 2, and 3 are referenced but not provided in the PDF. These supplements contain individual study characteristics, intervention details, and scanning parameters that are relevant for complete data extraction.

The number of participants in the FCP replication dataset is not explicitly stated in the main text. The FCP Cambridge Buckner dataset typically contains approximately 198 participants, but this was not confirmed in the paper and is not extracted.

The study does not include a sham acupuncture arm. Acupoint specificity is tested by comparing ST36 vs. GB34 networks (two real acupoints with anatomical proximity but meridian distinction), not against a sham control. The term 'acupoint specificity' in this paper refers to differential network activation between ST36 and GB34.

The primary studies included in the systematic review spanned a wide publication period (inception to March 2025) and included studies using 1.5T (20 studies) and 3.0T (13 studies) MRI, with 2 studies not reporting scan field strength. The FCNM resting-state data were acquired exclusively at 3T (SLIM and FCP datasets).
